newsitem.title: USA: GASB to get two new members as key issues mount.
newsitem.headline: GASB to get two new members as key issues mount.

text.p: The foundation that oversees the activities of the Governmental Accounting Standards Board said it will increase the number of GASB members from five to seven.

The expansion announced by the Financial Accounting Foundation comes at a key time for GASB, a private-sector panel that sets financial accounting and reporting standards for state and local governments.
GASB is close to finalizing new standards that would require municipalities to value their investment portfolios at the current price at which assets can be bought or sold.
Currently, municipalities value investment holdings at the price they originally paid for them, revising that amount only when the localities sell the investments or they mature.

Foundation Chairman J. Michael Cook, chairman of the Financial Accounting Foundation, said in a press statement that one new member will be a "preparer" of state financial statements and the other will be a "user" of government financial statements in general.
"We haven't identified anyone yet," said GASB spokeswoman Deborah Harrington. "We want to get them on board by July 1, 1997," she said.
Cook said the additions "will bring a broader perspective to GASB deliberations."
In a related matter, the Government Finance Officers Association said it will hold its annual GAAP Update Seminar on November 18 between 1300 and 1700 EST via satellite telecast.

The video teleconference will cover new GASB guidelines on pension plans, upcoming draft standards on financial reporting by municipalities, and the soon-to-be-completed "fair market value" project. For further information, call Rosemary Buckley at 312-977-9700.
